title: 16lwti6
Imam Hasan, the peace treaty and Umayyad rule
hook: Imam Hasan, whom the Prophet called a sayyid, gave up his right so that the blood of the community would not be shed, and he was poisoned.
scenes.0.text: In Medina, in the Prophet's mosque, the congregation would gather in front of the pulpit. His grandson, **Hasan**, was sometimes present when the Prophet spoke. He was the first son of Fatimah and Ali and the Prophet was deeply attached to him. As the prophet spoke, he looked at a congregation and turned to his grandson. The congregation could see clearly in the Prophet's face his love for this child. The Prophet used to say about Hasan and his brother Husayn, "These two are the masters of the youth of Paradise". The people of Medina watched with love as the boy grew up with the Prophet.
scenes.0.art.actors.1.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.0.art.actors.2.label: 1bj9fo
Imam Hasan
scenes.1.text: One day, while he was in the pulpit, the Prophet pointed to **Hasan** and said to the congregation, "This is my son Sayyid. Allah will reconcile the two groups of the Muslims by it". Sayyid means master and leader. That's the word in Buhari. At that time, no one in the congregation knew when or how this would happen. But the Prophet foretold that his grandson would sign a peace treaty that would stop the bloodshed of the nation. Years later, Hasan's reconciliation would be remembered not as a defeat, but as a mercy heralded by his grandfather.
scenes.1.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.1.art.actors.1.label: 1bj9fo
Imam Hasan
scenes.2.text: In Medina, the congregation had lined up for prayer at the Prophet's Mosque. The Prophet came to the mosque with one of his grandchildren in his arms. The Sahabi Sheddad b. al-Had narrates that the child in the lap that day was **Hasan** or Husayn. The Prophet left the boy, took a bow and stopped praying. When he came to prostrate, the little grandson climbed on his back. The Prophet did not raise his head from the ground and prostrated himself more than usual. When Shaddad looked up in curiosity, he saw the child on the Prophet's back and bowed down again. And when the prayer was ended, they said, "We thought you had been made to prostrate". The Prophet replied, "None of that has happened. My son got on my back. I didn't want to rush him until he was done". Abu Hurayrah also recites a night prayer. That night, when the Prophet came to every prayer, Hasan and Husayn jumped on his back. And when he lifted his head, he took them both by the back of his hand and brought them down softly. When he returned to prostrate, the two brothers came up on his back again. After the prayer, he got them on their knees. When Abu Hurayrah offered to take the children to their mothers, lightning struck in the sky. He said to them, "Go to your mother". The two brothers walked by the lightning and came to **Fatima**.
scenes.2.art.actors.1.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.2.art.actors.2.label: 1bj9fo
Imam Hasan
scenes.2.art.actors.3.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.3.text: In the 40th year of the Hijrah, during the month of Ramadan, **Ali** was martyred in the Kufa mosque. After the funeral, the people of Kufa made a vow to his eldest son, **Hasan**. A pledge of allegiance. Hasan became the new Imam of the Ummah by his father's will. When he went up to the minbar in the Kufa mosque, his face showed the grief of a son who lost his father. His father's blood had not yet dried up and the entire burden of the nation was now on his shoulders. But there was still a non-believing governor in Damascus, and the Imamate of Hasan would be tested from day one.
scenes.3.art.actors.1.label: 1bj9fo
Imam Hasan
scenes.4.text: In Damascus, Mu'awiya controlled trade routes and a wealthy treasure. Taking advantage of Ali's testimony, he gathered his army and marched on Kufa. **Hasan** prepared his army and marched in the opposite direction. As the two armies drew closer, it became clear that a new civil war between the Muslims was imminent. And the coffin was split. The fatigue of Jamal, Siffin and Nahrawan had fallen on the people. Soon after his father's martyrdom, Hasan was on the brink of a second great war.
scenes.4.art.actors.1.label: 1inzbgl
Mu'awiya
scenes.5.text: Mu'awiya began to bribe **Hasan**'s commanders before the war with trickery and bribes. Ubaydullah b. Abbas, one of Hasan's commanders, left his army one night and secretly crossed over to Mu'awiya's side. Then others followed him. The army was rotting from the inside. Hasan saw that if he went into battle with a weak army, the Ahl al-Bayt would be defeated in vain. He stopped the war so that the blood of the nation would not be shed and the loyal people would not perish. Thus, in 41 AH, the rule passed to Mu'awiya. Mu'awiya and his supporters called it "Amu'l-Jamaa", or "Year of Unity", saying that the nation was now united under one ruler. Yet this unity was built on the silence of bribed commanders and a dispersed army.
scenes.5.art.actors.0.label: 1bj9fo
Imam Hasan
scenes.5.art.actors.1.label: 1inzbgl
Mu'awiya
scenes.6.text: When the peace treaty was signed, **Hasan** imposed important conditions. The Mu'awiya would rule by the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of the Prophet, would not harm anyone and would not appoint a c**aliph** after him. Hasan did not renounce his right to imamate under these conditions. He only gave up his rule to protect the blood of the nation. But the Deputy didn't meet any of those requirements. Before the ink of reconciliation had dried, the curse of Ali was pronounced in the pulpits. The treaty was on paper, but it was re-breached every Friday in his sermon.
scenes.6.art.actors.0.label: 1bj9fo
Imam Hasan
scenes.7.text: After the peace treaty **Imam Hasan** left Kufa and returned to Medina. There, in his grandfather's city, he lived a quiet life for about ten years. **Mu'awiya**, however, wanted to make his son **Yazid** caliph after him. The greatest obstacle on that path was Imam Hasan, who knew the terms of the treaty and carried the love of the people. Mu'awiya secretly sent word to Imam Hasan's wife **Ja'da bint al-Ash'ath**. He promised that if she poisoned Imam Hasan, he would marry her to his son Yazid and give her a hundred thousand dirhams. Ja'da was taken in by this promise and gave her husband the poison Mu'awiya had sent. Imam Hasan suffered for about forty days and then passed away. His death is given as 28 Safar 49 or 50. According to a narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, the one who poisoned Imam Hasan was Ja'da. When Imam Hasan was martyred, Mu'awiya did not keep his word. Ja'da neither married Yazid nor received all of the promised money. In this way the last obstacle before Yazid's succession was removed by Mu'awiya's hand.
scenes.7.art.actors.0.label: 1bj9fo
Imam Hasan
scenes.7.art.actors.1.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.8.text: While on his deathbed, **Hasan** called his brother Husayn and made a will to him. He asked to be buried with his grandfather, the Messenger of Allah. But on one condition: "Not a drop of blood will be spilled at my funeral". If he is prevented from being buried next to the Prophet and there is a danger of bloodshed, he ordered that he be buried at the Baku cemetery, next to his grandmother Fatima bint Ased. Hasan had predicted that he would be prevented from being buried next to the Prophet. The imam who gave up his right to protect the blood of the nation during his life showed the same compassion even in death.
scenes.8.art.actors.0.label: 1bj9fo
Imam Hasan
scenes.8.art.actors.1.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.9.text: **Imam Husayn** and the Banu Hashim lifted Imam Hasan's coffin onto their shoulders and walked toward the Prophet's grave. At that very moment **Aisha**, riding a mule, blocked the way together with **Marwan** and the Umayyads. She did not allow the coffin to be buried beside the Prophet. Marwan too shouted, "While Uthman is buried in al-Baqi, is Hasan to be buried in the Prophet's house?" On Aisha's order, arrows were shot at the coffin of the Prophet's grandson. Seeing this, **Ibn Abbas** could not hold back and said to Aisha: "One day you ride a camel, one day a mule." At the Camel she had ridden a camel against Imam Ali, and now she had ridden a mule against Imam Hasan's funeral.
scenes.9.art.actors.0.label: sbbh7k
Marwan
scenes.9.art.actors.1.label: rrckkf
Aisha
scenes.9.art.actors.2.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.10.text: Mervan's men obeyed his orders and shot the coffin. The arrows were aimed at the coffin that carried the body of the Prophet's grandson, whom he called Sayyid. Some stories say the arrows were fired by the Emevi. One legend says that seventy arrows struck the coffin, but that number is given only in one source. Regardless of the number of arrows, the Prophet's grandson's funeral was met with arrows in his grandfather's hometown. As the coffin-carriers waited furiously under the arrows, everyone's eyes turned to Husayn standing beside his brother's coffin.
scenes.10.art.actors.1.label: 1bj9fo
Imam Hasan
scenes.11.text: He didn't draw Husayn's sword and told his sons not to either. He remembered his brother's will: "Not a drop of blood shall be shed at my funeral". The coffin was turned back from the Prophet's tomb and taken to the Baku cemetery. **Hasan** was buried there alongside his grandmother Fatima bint Ased. A large crowd had gathered at the funeral and the people of Medina were weeping. When Husayn gave his brother to the earth, he fulfilled his will to the letter. Not a drop of blood was spilled that day. The tomb of Hasan is still in Medina, in the Baku cemetery.
scenes.11.art.actors.0.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.12.text: Mu'awiya died in the 60th year of the Hijrah. Contrary to the terms of the truce, he left his son Yazid as caliph before he died. So it became a dynasty passed down from father to son within a caliphal family. The last condition of Hasan's reconciliation was violated. Meanwhile, the Prophet's last surviving grandson, Husayn, was in Medina. His brother had given up his right to peace, but it was no longer the time to be silent in the face of Yazid's rule. Husayn refused to swear allegiance to Yazid, and this refusal was the beginning of the road that would lead him to Karbala.
scenes.12.art.actors.0.label: 1f4krkm
Yazid
scenes.12.art.actors.2.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
sunni.0.says: From Abu Bakra: The Prophet, on the pulpit with Imam Hasan beside him, says, "This son of mine is a sayyid; through him God will reconcile two great groups of Muslims." The report also tells of Imam Hasan's peace treaty with Mu'awiya.
sunni.1.says: A repetition of the same Abu Bakra report in other chapters is to be expected.
sunni.2.says: From Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn are the masters of the youth of Paradise.
sunni.3.says: The pledge of allegiance to Imam Hasan after Imam Ali's martyrdom, the confrontation with Mu'awiya and the handing over of rule.
sunni.4.says: That Imam Hasan was buried in al-Baqi' and a great crowd gathered at the funeral; it does not contain the matter of burial beside the Prophet and the obstruction.
sunni.4.grade: al-Waqidi is in the chain; generally regarded as weak by hadith scholars
sunni.5.says: It is reported that Aisha initially agreed to Imam Hasan's wish to be buried beside the Prophet.
sunni.6.says: Marwan's saying, "While Uthman is buried in al-Baqi', is Hasan to be buried in the Prophet's house?"
sunni.7.says: The account of Marwan's informing Mu'awiya and of the demands about the burial place.
sunni.8.says: The report that Aisha came on a mule and wanted the Hashimites to be prevented.
sunni.9.says: That the Umayyads shot arrows at Imam Hasan's funeral.
sunni.10.says: It is relayed "according to the report" that Ja'da was persuaded by the promise of marriage to Yazid and poisoned Imam Hasan.
sunni.11.says: He relays the account of the poisoning (the physician's saying that the intestines were torn to pieces, Imam Husayn's question "who did it?"), but rejects the report of Yazid's promise to Ja'da, saying "in my view it is not authentic, and even more remote in the case of Mu'awiya."
sunni.12.says: He says that it is not established by reliable evidence that Mu'awiya had him poisoned, and that speaking on this matter would be speaking without knowledge.
sunni.13.says: It is relayed that some early Sunni historians (according to Madelung) attributed the poison to Mu'awiya; that al-Waqidi attributed the poison to a servant acting on Mu'awiya's behalf.
sunni.14.says: From Shaddad b. al-Had: the Prophet came to prayer carrying Imam Hasan or Imam Husayn and prolonged the prostration; when asked, he said, "My son climbed onto my back, and I did not want to hurry him until he had finished."
sunni.15.says: A parallel of Shaddad's report; and from Abu Hurayra: at the isha prayer, when the Prophet prostrated, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn would leap onto his back and he would set them down gently; after the prayer he sat them on his lap, and when lightning flashed he said, "Go to your mother."
sunni.15.grade: Editors: chain of 16033 sahih, chain of 10659 hasan
sunni.16.says: Abu Hurayra's report of the isha prayer: Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn leap onto the Prophet's back in prostration, and after the prayer they go to their mother in the light of the lightning.
shia.0.says: Biat to Hasan, peace with Mu'awiya and the legend that Hasan was poisoned and martyred.
shia.1.says: The blocking of the way, Imam Husayn's prevention of bloodshed, and Imam Hasan's burial beside his grandmother; Marwan's words.
shia.2.says: That arrows were shot at the funeral and seventy arrows struck; this detail has been found only in this source.
shia.3.says: The tension over the burial and Imam Hasan's will.
shia.4.says: The report that Imam Hasan said in advance that Aisha would obstruct.
shia.5.says: That Mu'awiya came to an agreement with Ja'da and had Imam Hasan poisoned with the promise of money and marriage to Yazid; that the death occurred about forty days later.
shia.6.says: From Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq: The one who poisoned Imam Hasan is Ja'da.
shia.7.says: It is said that Mu'awiya gave the poison to Ju'de.
shia.8.says: The words attributed to Mu'awiya: "I fear you will do to my son what you did to the Prophet's son with poison".
shia.9.says: It is reported that Husayn took his brother to the Prophet, that Aisha came with a mule and prevented the coffin from being buried there and gave the arrow order, that Mervan's men shot the coffin with this order, that Ibn Abbas said "one day a camel, one day a mule" and that Hasan was buried in Baku on the will of Husayn that no blood be spilled.
shia.10.says: It is reported that Mu'awiya poisoned Hasan by promising marriage to Yazid and one hundred thousand dirhams to Jude bint Esh'as, but did not keep his promise.
shia.11.says: When the Prophet prolonged his prostration, Imam Hasan was on his shoulder; he said, "Revelation did not come to me; my son was on my shoulder, and I did not want to hurry him until he came down." The words "my son climbed onto my back" from Shaddad's report are also relayed.
disputes.0.title: 143aevt
How is the peace treaty read?
disputes.0.sunni: It is said that the two groups reconciled with the reconciliation of Hasan. This event is also mentioned in Sunni sources (Buhari, No. 2704), which is a very good example. In Sunni reading, this is its virtue and the unity of the Ummah.
disputes.0.shia: It is said that the two groups reconciled with the reconciliation of Hasan. This event is also mentioned in Sunni sources (Buhari, No. 2704), which is a very good example. In the Shiite narrative, he did not give up that right, the conditions were later changed.
disputes.1.title: 1jf3g0w
Who poisoned Imam Hasan?
disputes.1.sunni: That Imam Hasan was poisoned appears in many sources, and Ja'da's name is mentioned. Ibn Taymiyya and Ibn Kathir say that Mu'awiya's order is not established by authentic evidence.
disputes.1.shia: That Imam Hasan was poisoned appears in many sources, and Ja'da's name is mentioned. In Shia books Mu'awiya is held to have had him poisoned for Yazid's path; Imam Hasan is a martyr.
disputes.2.title: 19ofwqm
Why was the burial not beside the Prophet?
disputes.2.sunni: It is told that Imam Hasan wished to be buried beside the Prophet. In the Sunni reading the room was at Aisha's disposal; there was concern about strife (fitna), and it is stressed that the real objection came from Marwan.
disputes.2.shia: It is told that Imam Hasan wished to be buried beside the Prophet. In the Shia account, Aisha herself prevented the coffin from being buried beside the Prophet and gave the order for arrows. Marwan's men shot with this order. Imam Husayn did not draw his sword because of the will that blood not be shed.
disputes.3.title: 19r0ddp
Who shot the arrows?
disputes.3.sunni: He's tied to the Emevils in Dineveri, where the arrow was thrown at the funeral. The Shi'a narration (al-Irshad, Bihar; page number not given) states that Aisha personally prevented and gave the order to shoot.
disputes.3.shia: Aisha gave the order for arrows. Marwan's men shot at the coffin, and the arrows stuck in the coffin. Ibn Shahrashub says seventy arrows; this number rests on a single source.
disputes.4.title: 88iswv
The masters of the youth of Paradise
disputes.4.sunni: It is a great virtue for Hasan and Husayn to be called the masters of the youth of Paradise. This event also occurs in Sunni sources (Tirmizi, No. 3768). In Sunni reading, this word does not rule out imamate.
disputes.4.shia: It is a great virtue for Hasan and Husayn to be called the masters of the youth of Paradise. This event also occurs in Sunni sources (Tirmizi, No. 3768). In the Shia narrative, this word is mentioned along with the spiritual leadership of the Ehl-i Beyt.
questions.0: Most early sources report that Hasan was poisoned. Why do you think Hasan was the biggest obstacle to making Yazid, Muawi's son, caliph?
questions.1: When his grandfather Hasan wanted to be buried next to the Prophet, he stipulated that "not a drop of blood be spilled at my funeral". Why do you think Hasan made this condition?
questions.2: When an arrow was thrown at Hasan's coffin, Husayn did not draw his sword. Why do you think Husayn didn't draw his sword even under the arrows?
questions.3: The Prophet said of Hasan: "By him Allah will reconcile the two great groups of Muslims". Why do you think the Prophet preached this peace, not as a defeat, but as good news?
questions.4: The Prophet said of the two brothers, "the masters of the youth of Paradise". Why do you think that Hasan's resignation for peace and Husayn's refusal to swear allegiance to Yazid make sense?
questions.5: The terms of the peace treaty and the death are told differently in the books. In such a place, which account would you trust, and why?
questions.6: Hazrat Hasan had insisted that Mu'awiya not appoint him as caliph after him on the terms of peace, and Mu'awiya left his son Yazid in his place. How do you think the violation of this condition explains why Husayn refused to swear allegiance to Yazid?
summary: Hasan, whom the Prophet called a seyyid, took the oath after his father's martyrdom. When the Mu'awiya bribed the army to disband, Hasan ended the war to avoid bloodshed. The terms of the peace were later violated. About ten years later, he was martyred by poisoning.
notes.0: The Prophet said of Imam Hasan, «this son of mine is a sayyid» (al-Bukhari 2704).
notes.1: After Imam Ali's martyrdom, the pledge of allegiance was given to Imam Hasan.
notes.2: Hasan ended the war to avoid bloodshed after the army was bought. Management has passed to the Mu'awiya. The terms of the peace were later violated. This year was called the Year of Unity.
notes.3: He lived in Medina for about ten years and was martyred by poison.
notes.4: It is also mentioned in the history books that Hasan was poisoned. He's a martyr at the Jaffrey school.
notes.5: At the funeral, Aisha herself prevented the coffin from being buried beside the Prophet and gave the order for arrows. Marwan's men shot at the coffin. Imam Husayn did not draw his sword. Imam Hasan was buried in al-Baqi' (al-Irshad, Bihar).
